ops: repo-memory: Read/Write/Glob/Edit only (Bash/Grep on /tmp blocked). Bash sandbox's 'don't ask mode' denies `for` loops and some `&&`/redirect chains outright (not just prompts), even read-only ones against /tmp or the repo - issue one gh api call per id instead of looping. A single `cmd1 | cmd2` pipe DOES work. Use the Grep/Read tools instead of bash loops wherever possible.

create issue RECIPE: Write eslint-factory/.tmp_issue_body.md, then `jq -Rs '{title,body:.,labels:["eslint","eslint-factory"]}' file.md | safeoutputs create_issue .` directly (no intermediate json file, skips the rm step that gets denied).

dedupe: `gh api "search/issues?q=repo:github/gh-aw+label:eslint-factory+is:issue+is:open"` is the reliable zero-state check (the plain issues?state=open&labels= REST form intermittently returns empty/null even when issues exist - use the search/issues endpoint and read total_count, the nested items[0].items[] shape is a known API quirk, don't be confused by it). `gh api issues/<n> --jq '{state,state_reason}'` for history, one id per call (loops blocked).

`gh api pulls/<PR#>/files --jq '.[].filename'` (PR# from HEAD commit's '(#NNNNN)') is the real changed-file list, immune to the shallow-clone all-insertions squash artifact (git log/blame on rules/ confirmed dead 16+ runs).

eslint-factory: no node_modules/dist, npm firewalled, no live lint - ground via Grep on non-test .cjs + rule src/tests. Check for existing eslint-disable-next-line before concluding ungrounded. ALWAYS re-read current rule source + its .test.ts before refiling an expired theme - rules get fixed without the issue being closed as completed (confirmed multiple times), and conversely issues DO get closed completed when genuinely fixed (today: 3 in one day) - always verify source, never assume either direction from bot state alone.

Rule-name history search gotcha: combined-rule-review entries sometimes name multiple rules in one shorthand string (e.g. 09-14's 'no-core-error-then-setfailed/process-exit/process-exitcode') that a literal per-rule-name grep misses - before concluding a rule was 'never reviewed', also grep for its distinguishing substrings/keywords, not just the exact hyphenated name.

Issues auto-expire ~1wk TTL typically bot-closed not_planned regardless of fix status - verify source before assuming 'still broken'. But genuine fixes CAN also get closed completed directly (today's 3 are the first clean confirmed cluster of this). Retire a theme after 2 expiries with no source change, OR immediately upon confirming a completed-closure fix in source.
